question: I've been experiencing joint pain and stiffness for weeks. My hands and knees mostly hurt in the morning, but I feel tired all the time. I'm worried that it could be rheumatoid arthritis. 3. Give five sharp blows between their shoulder blades using the heel of your hand. Count out loud while keeping one arm around them to support.

4. After the 5th hit, give 5 firm abdominal thrusts (like giving them a big hug from behind). Each squeeze should be firm enough to try to force out the stuck object; keep going until you've done 5.

5. If after both sets, the object doesn’t come out, call emergency services. Keep going with the above steps until help arrives or if the person becomes unconscious.

6. If they’ve become unconscious or unresponsive, place them on the floor, kneel beside them, lift their chin to open their airway fully before delivering several quick chest compressions as hard as you can (this will vary for individuals).

7. Check once more if the object has come out and clear their mouth. If not yet, continue to provide chest compressions.

8. Once help arrives, stay calm and reassure the individual who may be shaken.

It’s essential to remember how serious choking can be, so learning this technique can make a life-saving difference if needed. Good luck teaching your family!
